Addressed in ab7dc5d978. Each finding was verified against the code before fixing:

**1. Reconnects do not resweep — fixed.** Verified the stream never replays: `createClientConnection.connect()` calls `api.event.subscribe()` with no cursor or `Last-Event-ID`, and every reconnect starts fresh at `server.connected` (`packages/client/src/solid/connection.ts:73-89`). The sweep effect now tracks `sdk.connection.status()` and reruns on every `connected` transition.

**2. Unloaded servers are not swept — fixed.** Verified `data.session.list()` is just `Object.values(store.session.info)` (`packages/client/src/solid/data.ts:209`), populated only by explicit syncs or events. The sweep now inventories `session.active()`, which is server-wide — the handler has no `Location` dependency (`packages/server/src/handlers/session.ts:141-147`) and delegates to the process-global execution coordinator (`packages/core/src/session.ts:870`). Unknown IDs are resolved with `data.session.sync(id)` (fetch-by-ID, `data.ts:1322`). This inventory is complete because a pending request can only belong to an active execution: `Permission.assert` wraps `Deferred.await` with `Effect.ensuring(pending.delete(...))` (`packages/core/src/permission.ts:251-255`), so interruption clears the entry. The one exception is the external `session.permission.create` API, which creates a detached pending entry via `Permission.ask` — it has no in-repo caller and its `permission.asked` event still covers it while connected; a request created that way on an *idle* session during a disconnect remains the only unswept case.

**3. Sweeps discard `workspaceID` — fixed.** Locations now deduplicate on `directory + workspaceID` and the query passes `{ directory, workspace: location.workspaceID }`. Wire format verified: the server parses `location[workspace]` (`packages/server/src/location.ts:31`), the generated client serializes nested query objects as `key[child]` and skips `undefined` (`packages/client/src/promise/generated/client.ts:1881-1893`), and `PermissionRequestListInput` names the field `workspace` while `SessionInfo.location` carries `workspaceID`.

**4. Failed reply invisible — bounded retry added.** `approve` retries up to 2 more times with linear backoff, re-checking `disposed`/`enabled` before each retry. After exhaustion the deduplication entry is removed, so any later sweep (reconnect, re-enable) retries the request.

**5. Unbounded `responded` set — capped.** Insertion-order eviction above 1000 entries, matching the bound the old implementation used.

**Testing gap — covered.** `remote-session-settings.spec.ts` now:
- test 1: server A has no tab and is never visited, holds a pre-seeded pending request, and the mock `session.active` reports its sessions running; the toggle on server B's settings must produce exactly one `reply: "once"` POST to server A (`toEqual`, not `toContainEqual`).
- new test 3: after toggling on and completing an initial sweep, a pending request is seeded while `transport.disconnect()` severs the stream (never delivered as an event); the assertion requires the reconnect sweep alone to reply to it.

All 3 e2e tests pass, plus `bun typecheck`, `typecheck:e2e`, and the 42 unit tests.

All four points addressed in b702e2a:

**1. Stale positive memo — fixed with eviction on dead-repo detection.** Added `repoRun(repository, args)` in `packages/core/src/git.ts` wrapping the repository probe commands (remote/rootCommits/head/branch/remoteHead). When a run fails with the spawn-failure signature (exitCode != 0 and empty stderr — the `run` wrapper collapses spawn ENOENT into exactly that) or git's own `not a git repository`, the discover memo evicts every entry matching that repository's `gitDirectory` or `worktree` (worktree match covers GIT_DIR relocation). Worst case for a false positive is one re-discovery (3 spawns) — i.e. pre-PR behavior — so the heuristic is safe to over-fire.

**2. Single-flight key — fixed both ways.** Key is now `${cwd}\0${JSON.stringify(args)}` (no "a b" vs ["a","b"] collision), and runs with `opts.env !== undefined` are excluded from sharing entirely, per your second option — one future GIT_DIR caller can't receive another caller's output.

**3. Degrade trigger — gated on the untracked subset, as required.** `value.filter((item) => item.status === "added").length > UNTRACKED_DEGRADE_AT`. In this codebase `??` maps to `"added"` (`packages/opencode/src/git/index.ts` `kind()`), so the gate now counts exactly the entries whose enumeration is pathological under `--untracked-files=all`. A repo with thousands of tracked modifications no longer gets persisted into `vcs-degraded.json`. Comment updated to say so.

**4. EOL churn — root-caused and fixed.** The two test files had been saved with CRLF (Windows editor); restored to LF. The cumulative PR diff for them is now +89 lines of actual new tests, nothing else.

Verification: `bun test test/git/git.test.ts test/project/vcs.test.ts` (25 pass), `bun test test/git.test.ts` in core (4 pass), typecheck clean in both packages.

**2.** Added `packages/core/test/script-migration.test.ts`: two cases covering name derivation and sort order via a real `Bun.Glob` scan of a temp fixture (exercising the platform-native separator — backslash on Windows, forward slash on Linux/macOS). This required guarding the script's top-level `await generate()` with `import.meta.main` so it's importable without side effects; CLI behavior is unchanged.

Verified: new tests pass, `bun run script/migration.ts --check` exits 0 on Windows (previously the ENOENT path), typecheck clean.

Independent confirmation on 1.18.21 (npm binary, Linux x64) with a **minimal single-plugin repro** — no Discord RPC or concurrency needed to demonstrate the loss mechanism:

**Repro**
1. `.opencode/plugin/stall.ts`:
```ts
import type { Plugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"
export const StallPlugin: Plugin = async () => ({
  "chat.message": async () => {
    await new Promise(() => {}) // never settles
  },
})
```
2. Start server with the plugin loaded (`STALL_HOOK=1` gates the stall inside the hook).
3. `POST /session` → `POST /session/:id/prompt_async` (returns **204**) → wait → `GET /session/:id/message`.

| run | messages persisted |
|---|---|
| stalling hook enabled | **0** |
| same plugin, hook body no-ops (control) | 2 (user + assistant) |

So a single hung hook is sufficient; loss is deterministic, not a burst/race artifact. Matches the diagnosis: `Plugin.trigger` runs hooks via `Effect.promise(...)` (`packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts`, non-interruptible, no deadline), and the `"chat.message"` trigger in `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts` runs *before* `sessions.updateMessage(info)` — so the fiber parks after the API acknowledged, before persistence.

**Fix direction** that would close both halves:
1. Wrap per-hook dispatch as interruptible and raced against a per-hook deadline (log-and-skip on timeout), mirroring what the TUI runtime already does with its hard 5s dispose budget.
2. Reorder `prompt.ts` so `sessions.updateMessage(info)` / `updatePart` happen before the `chat.message` trigger (or make trigger failure/hang non-fatal to persistence) — a prompt the API acknowledged with 204 should never end up with zero message rows.

Happy to test a patch.

All three findings verified as valid and addressed in fb7f250cbe.

**1. Retry after disable — fixed.** Confirmed the gap: the catch checked `enabled()` before *scheduling* the retry, but disabling during the 1–2s backoff still let the fired timer approve. `approve()` now rechecks `enabled()` in its initial guard, making it the single authoritative check for every entry path (event, sweep, retry timer); the redundant pre-scheduling check was removed.

**2. Idle detached requests — mitigated.** Confirmed the path: `session.permission.create` calls `Permission.ask`, which registers a pending entry with no awaiting fiber (`packages/core/src/permission.ts:224-229`), unlike `assert` whose entry dies with its fiber. The sweep inventory is now the union of active-session locations and locally known session locations (`data.session.list()`), so a detached request on any session this client has loaded is recovered. The remaining uncovered case — a detached request on a session this client has never loaded — would need a server-wide pending-request inventory endpoint (a protocol + server + generated-client change). Since `session.permission.create` has no in-repo caller and its live `permission.asked` event is still handled while connected, I left that endpoint out as disproportionate; happy to add it if external usage materializes. The residual case is documented in the module comment.

**3. Sweep failures — bounded retry added.** A sweep now reports completeness: `session.active` failure, any session-resolution failure, or any per-location listing failure marks it incomplete, and the effect retries up to 2 more times with linear backoff. A generation counter makes newer sweeps (reconnect, re-enable) supersede scheduled retries, and the timer rechecks `disposed`/`enabled` before rerunning.

**Coverage.** The reconnect e2e test now also injects a 500 on the first `/api/permission/request` after the reconnect, so the assertion can only pass through the bounded sweep retry. All 3 e2e tests, 42 unit tests, and both typechecks pass.

Thanks for the correction on the exhausted-retry finding. The three remaining findings are all valid and addressed in 7163804c8f.

**1. High: stale locations for moved active sessions — fixed.** Confirmed the mechanism: `data.session.sync(id)` is a no-op for already-synced sessions because `sync.run` returns immediately once the key is complete (`packages/client/src/solid/data.ts:156-161`), so a cached location was never refreshed. The sweep now calls `data.session.invalidate(id)` before `sync(id)` for *every* active session, so each sweep lists permissions from fresh locations. A failed resync falls back to the cached location for that pass and marks the sweep incomplete, so the bounded retry re-attempts. The reconnect e2e test now asserts that `/api/session/:id` is re-fetched after the reconnect.

**2. Medium: idle detached requests / late discovery — fixed for everything the client can see.** Added a reactive effect that approves any pending request present in the local store (`store.session.permission`), which is exactly how a previously unknown idle session's requests surface: opening its view runs `data.session.permission.sync(id)`. This closes the "request is visible to the client but hidden by the setting and never approved" hole, and it needs no network. New e2e test: a request served only from `/api/session/:id/permission` (never from a location sweep or an event) is approved once auto-approve is on. The residual case — a detached request on a session this client has never loaded — still requires a server-wide pending-request inventory endpoint; my position from the previous round is unchanged (no in-repo caller of `session.permission.create`, disproportionate protocol change), but I'm happy to add the endpoint if you want it in this PR.

**3. Medium: reply mock returned 200 instead of 204 — fixed.** Confirmed against the generated client: `session.permission.reply` declares `successStatus: 204` and `request()` rejects any other status (`packages/client/src/promise/generated/client.ts:1439`, `:297`). The mock now fulfills the reply route with a bare 204, so every reply assertion in the spec now proves a *successful* approval; previously each mocked reply failed client-side and the assertions only observed the attempt.

All 4 e2e tests, 42 unit tests, and both typechecks pass.

Thanks — both points are answerable, one with a citation and one with a commit.

### 1. The field is OpenAI's own, documented, with that exact example

Not a zen-side gateway invention. From OpenAI's prompt-caching guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching):

> For the Responses API, both fields appear in `usage.input_tokens_details`

and the worked example the code comment is pointing at:

```json
"input_tokens": 2600,
"input_tokens_details": { "cached_tokens": 2000, "cache_write_tokens": 400 }
```

> In this example, 2,000 tokens were read from the cache and 400 additional tokens were written. The remaining 200 input tokens were neither read nor written.

So `cache_write_tokens` is a first-class documented field, it lives in `input_tokens_details` alongside `cached_tokens`, and **both** are subsets of `input_tokens` — which is precisely what the current code got wrong by adding the write bucket on top. 2600 − 2000 − 400 = 200 uncached, not 2600 − 2000 = 600.

You're right that this reads as Anthropic-shaped accounting; the difference is that Anthropic puts its cache buckets *outside* `input_tokens` and OpenAI puts them *inside*. Same three numbers, opposite containment — which is exactly the trap this PR is about.

The same page also independently supports the double-billing half of the fix:

> A longer cache write does not bill the already cached 2,000 tokens again.

No comment or PR-body change needed, but if you'd prefer the doc URL inlined at `openai.ts:54-58` rather than the prose "OpenAI's own sample", say the word and I'll add it.

### 2. Already extended — 73c2363

Pushed after your review: `packages/console/app/test/providerUsage.test.ts:113`, `test("every helper partitions the prompt into the same four buckets")`. Same 2,600-token prompt expressed three ways, asserting both the uncached remainder and the four-bucket sum:

| helper | wire shape | expected `inputTokens` | four buckets sum to |
|---|---|---|---|
| openai | cache buckets **inside** `input_tokens` | 200 | 2600 |
| anthropic | cache buckets **outside** `input_tokens` | 200 | 2600 |
| google | no cache-write bucket at all | 600 | 2600 |

Google lands at 600 legitimately — `cachedContentTokenCount` has no write counterpart, so the 400 has nowhere to go but the uncached bucket. That asymmetry is the reason the guard is written against the normalized values rather than per-helper: `handler.ts` sums the same four fields for every provider when it picks the long-context tier, so normalized is the only place all three are required to agree.

One helper I deliberately left out: `openai-compatible.ts`. It subtracts `cacheReadTokens` from `inputTokens` but not `cacheWriteTokens`, so whether the partition holds depends on whether the upstream provider counts `cache_creation_input_tokens` inside `prompt_tokens` — and that varies per provider behind that adapter. Its `adjustCacheUsage` path also synthesizes a 90% cache-read share when the field is absent, which would make a sum-to-prompt assertion vacuous. Pinning a single answer there felt like a behaviour claim I can't source, unlike the three above. Happy to add it as a documented-expectation test if you'd rather have the current behaviour locked down.

Confirmed at source level on current main (41616958). In `processCompaction` (packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts) the model override correctly resolves the compaction agent:

```ts
const agent = yield* agents.get("compaction")
const model = agent.model ? ... : ...
```

but the assistant message a few lines below still hardcodes `variant: userMessage.model.variant`, so the compaction agent's own `variant` config is never consulted — the request inherits the triggering message's variant instead.

Minimal fix shape: resolve variant from the compaction agent config when set, falling back to `userMessage.model.variant` (~5 LOC), plus one test asserting variant resolution mirrors model resolution. Happy to open a PR if maintainers agree with this direction.

Confirmed still reproducible on current main (41616958). Two touch points in packages/llm/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts:

1. `OpenAIChatDelta` (line ~146) declares only `reasoning_content` — the Schema decode strips any unknown key, so a provider emitting `delta.reasoning` loses it before `step()` runs.
2. `step()` (line ~419) reads only `delta.reasoning_content`.

Fix shape: add `reasoning: optionalNull(Schema.String)` to the delta struct and coalesce in step() (`delta.reasoning ?? delta.reasoning_content`). ~10 LOC plus an SSE fixture test covering both field names. This also covers vLLM/SGLang and OpenRouter's `reasoning` field, not just Scaleway.

Note: PR #35284 for this issue was closed by automated cleanup without merge — happy to pick this up with a fresh minimal PR if that direction is acceptable.

Thanks for the detailed diagnostics — the id divergence you show (SQLite row `771729...` vs legacy JSON project file `7f7996...` for the same worktree) pins this to path normalization differing between the JSON-era project-id derivation and the SQLite migrator: one hashed a normalized forward-slash path, the other the raw Windows backslash form, so every session keyed under the old project id is skipped silently.

Two suggestions that would make the fix robust rather than point:

1. In the migrator, derive/lookup project ids by trying both raw and normalized forms of the worktree before skipping.
2. Fail loud instead of silent: report a count of unmigrated legacy sessions at startup so users know data exists but wasn't imported.

This should be unit-testable cross-platform with synthetic legacy-storage fixtures (no Windows machine needed). Happy to help with a PR if maintainers want it.

Still reproduces on **v1.18.21** (Windows 11, latest as of 2026-08-24), and I captured the underlying server-side error — confirming this is not a provider/network/auth outage.

## Clean reproduction

1. Create a project folder.
2. Have a conversation so the session is persisted
3. Rename the folder outside of OpenCode
4. Restart Desktop, reopen the session, send any prompt

The prompt appears in chat, processing terminates almost immediately, and no response or error is shown anywhere in the UI.

## Recovery test

Renaming the folder back to its original name immediately restores normal behavior — **without restarting Desktop**. This confirms the failure is tied purely to the stale saved project path, not to session state or the model.

## Server-side evidence

`~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` at the moment of the failed prompt:

```text
level=ERROR message=failed ref=err_fbcf70d0
error="PlatformError: NotFound: FileSystem.realPath (<the project folder>)
(cause: Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory,
lstat '<the project folder>"
```

Failure chain: stale project directory → `FileSystem.realPath()` → `ENOENT` → prompt request dies → UI shows nothing.

Agreed with the report: end of the chain looks exactly like a model/provider outage to users. A UI banner such as "This project directory no longer exists — reopen the project from an existing directory" would resolve the whole class of confusion.

Fresh data point from a fully-autonomous primary agent use case (v1.18.21, Linux x64, agent defined in `~/.config/opencode/agent/yolo.md`).

## Repro summary

Agent frontmatter set every tool-level category to `allow` but initially **omitted `external_directory`** (it is easy to miss — the key only appears in the config schema, and the default is `ask`):

- One day of use: **32 `external_directory` ask-events vs 3,513 allow-events**
- Asks fired for ordinary paths: `/tmp/*` writes and `/sys/bus/usb/devices/.../*` reads via bash
- Log lines: `evaluated permission=external_directory pattern=/tmp/* action.permission=external_directory action.pattern=* action.action=ask`

Adding `external_directory: allow` explicitly to the agent frontmatter stopped the asks in that scope, but the underlying expectation mismatch remains: users writing partial permission blocks for autonomous agents reasonably assume tool-level allows cover command side-effects on external paths.

## Two friction points worth addressing

1. **Discoverability**: `external_directory` is easy to omit because it is not obvious that bash commands touching /tmp or /sys count as "external directory" access. A prominent note in the agents/permissions docs would help.
2. **Override semantics**: if an agent explicitly sets `external_directory: allow`, users expect the documented "agent rules take precedence" behavior to hold without also needing a global-config rule.

I have opened #44657 documenting the complete all-keys block + this trap in the permissions docs. Happy to test any patch against the reproduction setup.

Adding independent reproduction data confirming this is still live and frequent on `v1.18.21` (macOS arm64) against **`opencode-go` / `ox-alpha-free`** — and that the missing raw finish reason has real diagnostic cost.

## Fresh evidence (one machine, logs + local sqlite)

**Escalating "Failed to drain Session" failures** (`The provider response ended with an unknown finish reason.`):

| day | occurrences |
|---|---|
| 2026-08-22 | 1 |
| 2026-08-23 | 4 |
| 2026-08-24 | 24 |

```
level=ERROR message="Failed to drain Session" cause="AI.Error: session.stream:
The provider response ended with an unknown finish reason.\n    at <anonymous> ...
at SessionRunner.runSteps ... at SessionRunner.drain"
```

**Persisted messages confirm the same shape as #41469:** querying the message store for all assistant turns:

```sql
SELECT json_extract(data,'$.finish'), COUNT(*)
FROM message WHERE json_extract(data,'$.role')='assistant'
GROUP BY 1;
-- tool-calls | 2633
-- stop       |  275
-- unknown    |   56   <-- ALL of these: tokens.output = 0, error field absent
```

All 56 `finish=unknown` rows are zero-output-token clean drains with no error field; **54 of 56 are `opencode-go/ox-alpha-free`** (2 are `deepseek-v4-flash`, same gateway). This build does not persist a `rawFinish` on the message row at all, so there is nothing to distinguish "content-filtered" from "gateway closed SSE early" — matching the observability gap described here.

**Gateway instability around the same window** (same provider/model): ~170 logged stream errors over Aug 21–22 (`AI_APICallError: Service Unavailable` ×161, `Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable.` ×7, `Internal Server Error` ×1), plus `Console Go: Upstream request failed` variants on Aug 24. Genuine special-cased `Provider finish_reason: network_error` errors: 2. So this model/gateway currently produces both failure families — thrown midstream errors (which retry correctly, up to 5 attempts with backoff before halting) and clean-empty drains that end as opaque `unknown`.

## Why surfacing the raw value matters here

With the current message, a user seeing 24 failures/day cannot tell whether ox-alpha-free is applying a server-side filter (the `rawFinish:"sensitive"` case above), rate-limiting via early EOF, or truncating streams under load — three very different remedies (rephrase vs. back off vs. report gateway bug). Appending the unrecognized raw string to this error (or mapping unrecognized values through the existing `network_error` special-case pattern) would immediately disambiguate.

Happy to provide redacted log excerpts or the sqlite dumps if useful.
